question:
Elements in the modern periodic table are arranged in ________ vertical columns.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 18
16
12
9
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 18

Explanation:
In the modern periodic table, elements are arranged in 18 vertical columns, known as 'groups'. This arrangement is the modern version of the periodic table proposed by Dmitri Mendeleev, which was later developed by Henry Moseley based on atomic number. Each group contains elements with similar chemical properties. The periodic table also has 7 horizontal rows (periods), which represent the electronic configuration of elements.

Extra Facts:
☛ The f-block elements (lanthanides and actinides) are shown separately at the bottom of the periodic table.
☛ Group 1 elements are called alkali metals, and Group 2 elements are called alkaline earth metals.
☛ Group 17 elements are known as halogens, and Group 18 elements are called noble gases.
☛ Metals, non-metals, and metalloids are located in distinct regions of the periodic table.

question:
The IUPAC name of an element is Unnilennium. What is the symbol of the element?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Une
Unl
Unm
Unu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Une

Explanation:
In the IUPAC nomenclature system, temporary names for elements are given based on their atomic numbers. The name 'Unnilennium' is composed of three parts: 'Un' (1), 'Nil' (0), and 'Enn' (9), representing 1, 0, and 9 respectively. Combining these gives the atomic number 109. The symbol for this element is 'Une', derived from the first letters of 'Unnilennium'. This element is now known as 'Meitnerium (Mt)', with atomic number 109.

Extra Facts:
IUPAC adopted the temporary naming system in 1978. In this system, specific prefixes are assigned to digits 0 to 9. For example, 'Un' (1), 'Bi' (2), 'Tri' (3), 'Quad' (4), etc. This system provides temporary names and symbols for newly discovered elements until their official names are assigned. Meitnerium (Mt) is named in honor of the Austrian physicist Lise Meitner.

question:
In 1812, who described the hypothesis that equal volumes of different gases contain an equal number of molecules?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: John Dalton
Albert Einstein
James Watt
Amedeo Avogadro
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Amedeo Avogadro

Explanation:
In 1812, the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro proposed the 'Avogadro's Hypothesis', which stated that 'equal volumes of different gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain the same number of molecules'. This hypothesis became a fundamental basis for molecular theory and was later termed 'Avogadro's Law'. This law helped in understanding the behavior of gases in chemistry and established the concept of the 'mole'. Avogadro's number (6.022 × 1023) is derived from this law, representing the number of molecules in one mole of a substance.

Extra Facts:
Avogadro's number (6.022 × 1023) is used in the unit 'mole' and is essential for stoichiometric calculations in chemistry. Avogadro's Law refined 'Dalton's Atomic Theory', clarifying that gases are composed of molecules, not just atoms. This law laid the foundation for modern chemistry and helped in understanding the properties of gases.

☛ What does the unit 'mole' measure? → Amount of substance

solution_hi:

Explanation:
1812 में, इटली के वैज्ञानिक एमेडियो अवोगाद्रो ने 'अवोगाद्रो की परिकल्पना' प्रस्तुत की, जिसमें कहा गया कि 'समान तापमान और दाब पर, विभिन्न गैसों के समान आयतन में अणुओं की संख्या समान होती है'। यह परिकल्पना आणविक सिद्धांत का एक महत्वपूर्ण आधार बनी और बाद में इसे 'अवोगाद्रो का नियम' कहा गया। इस नियम ने रसायन विज्ञान में गैसों के व्यवहार को समझने में मदद की और 'मोल' की अवधारणा को स्थापित किया। अवोगाद्रो की संख्या (6.022 × 1023) इसी नियम से जुड़ी है, जो एक मोल में उपस्थित अणुओं की संख्या को दर्शाती है।

Extra Facts:
अवोगाद्रो की संख्या (6.022 × 1023) को 'मोल' की इकाई में उपयोग किया जाता है। यह संख्या रसायन विज्ञान में स्टोइकोमेट्री (stoichiometry) की गणना के लिए आवश्यक है। अवोगाद्रो के नियम ने 'डाल्टन के परमाणु सिद्धांत' को और विकसित किया, जिसमें यह स्पष्ट किया गया कि गैसें अणुओं से बनी होती हैं, न कि केवल परमाणुओं से। इस नियम ने आधुनिक रसायन विज्ञान की नींव रखी और गैसों के गुणों को समझने में मदद की।

question:
The element with atomic number 59 lies in which block of the Periodic Table?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: The s-block
The f-block
The p-block
The d-block
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The f-block

Explanation:
The element with atomic number 59 is 'Praseodymium (Pr)', which belongs to the 'Lanthanide series'. In the Periodic Table, Lanthanides and Actinides are classified as 'f-block' elements because their outermost electrons enter the 'f-subshell'. The electronic configuration of Praseodymium is [Xe] 4f³ 6s², where 3 electrons are in the f-subshell. Hence, it lies in the f-block. In s, p, and d-block elements, the last electron enters the s, p, and d-subshells respectively, but in f-block elements, the f-subshell is filled.

Extra Facts:
1. 'f-block' elements are also called 'inner transition elements' because they exhibit transitional properties similar to d-block transition elements.
2. Both Lanthanides (atomic numbers 57-71) and Actinides (atomic numbers 89-103) belong to the f-block.
3. f-block elements often exhibit a +3 oxidation state because their 6s² and 4f¹ electrons are easily lost.
4. Due to the lanthanide contraction, f-block elements show similar properties, making them difficult to separate.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ How many elements are in the f-block? → 28 (14 Lanthanides + 14 Actinides)
☛ How many blocks are there in the Periodic Table? → 4 (s, p, d, f)
☛ What are d-block elements called? → Transition elements

3. f-ब्लॉक तत्वों में अक्सर +3 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था पाई जाती है, क्योंकि इनके 6s² और 4f¹ इलेक्ट्रॉन आसानी से निकल जाते हैं।
4. लैन्थेनाइड संकुचन के कारण, f-ब्लॉक तत्वों के गुणों में समानता पाई जाती है, जिससे इन्हें अलग करना मुश्किल होता है।

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Is² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁶ 4d⁸ 5s¹

Explanation:
Rhodium (Rh) has an atomic number of 45, meaning it has 45 electrons. Its electronic configuration is written following the Aufbau Principle, which states that electrons fill lower energy orbitals before higher ones. The electronic configuration of Rhodium is: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁶ 4d⁸ 5s¹. Here, the 4d orbital has 8 electrons and the 5s orbital has 1 electron because the 4d orbital is partially filled, providing stability. This configuration is crucial for understanding Rhodium's chemical properties.

Extra Facts:
Rhodium is a transition metal and a member of the platinum group. It is a rare and valuable metal used in catalytic converters and jewelry. Rhodium has a melting point of 1964°C and a boiling point of 3695°C. It is chemically less reactive and reacts slowly with acids. Rhodium is also used in electrical contacts and optical devices due to its high reflectivity and corrosion resistance.

रोडियम (Rh) का परमाणु क्रमांक 45 है, जिसका अर्थ है कि इसमें 45 इलेक्ट्रॉन होते हैं। इसका इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखते समय, हम 'ऑफबाऊ सिद्धांत' (Aufbau Principle) का पालन करते हैं, जिसके अनुसार इलेक्ट्रॉन निम्न ऊर्जा स्तर से उच्च ऊर्जा स्तर में भरे जाते हैं। रोडियम का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास है: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁶ 4d⁸ 5s¹। यहाँ, 4d ऑर्बिटल में 8 इलेक्ट्रॉन और 5s ऑर्बिटल में 1 इलेक्ट्रॉन होता है, क्योंकि 4d ऑर्बिटल आंशिक रूप से भरा होता है और यह स्थिरता प्रदान करता है। यह विन्यास रोडियम के रासायनिक गुणों को समझने में महत्वपूर्ण है।

Extra Facts:
रोडियम एक 'संक्रमण धातु' (Transition Metal) है और यह प्लैटिनम समूह का सदस्य है। यह बहुत ही दुर्लभ और मूल्यवान धातु है, जिसका उपयोग उत्प्रेरक (Catalytic Converters) और गहनों में किया जाता है। रोडियम का गलनांक 1964°C और क्वथनांक 3695°C होता है। यह रासायनिक रूप से कम सक्रिय होता है और अम्लों के साथ धीमी प्रतिक्रिया करता है। रोडियम का उपयोग विद्युत संपर्कों और ऑप्टिकल उपकरणों में भी किया जाता है।

question:

[RRB NTPC CBT]

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Silicon

Explanation:
Metalloids are elements that exhibit properties of both metals and non-metals. Silicon is a metalloid located in Group 14 of the periodic table. It acts as a semiconductor and is widely used in electronic devices. Lead (Pb) and Gold (Au) are metals, while Bromine (Br) is a non-metal that exists in a liquid state at room temperature.

Extra Facts:
Metalloids include Boron (B), Silicon (Si), Germanium (Ge), Arsenic (As), Antimony (Sb), and Tellurium (Te). These elements are semiconductors of electricity and are used in making transistors, diodes, and solar cells. Silicon is the second most abundant element in the Earth's crust and is found in the form of sand (SiO₂).

question:
Identify the number of electrons found in the outermost shell of halogen.

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Two
One
Five
Seven
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seven

Explanation:
Halogens (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine) have 7 electrons in their outermost shell. They belong to Group 17 of the periodic table and have a valency of 1, as they gain one electron to complete their octet. Halogens are highly reactive and form ionic compounds with metals (e.g., NaCl). Their high electronegativity allows them to easily attract electrons.

Extra Facts:
1. The term "halogen" comes from Greek words "Halo" (salt) and "Gen" (producer), as they form salts.
2. Fluorine is the most reactive halogen and reacts with glass, metals, and water.
3. Chlorine is used in water disinfection (e.g., bleaching powder).
4. Iodine deficiency causes Goitre, so iodine is added to salt.

question_hi:
हैलोजन के बाह्यतम कोश में पाए जाने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या की पहचान कीजिए।

question:
The behaviour of lithium is similar to that of magnesium. This sort of similarity is commonly referred to as:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: same Zeff
inert pair effect
isoelectronic species
diagonal relationship
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is diagonal relationship

Explanation:
The similarity between lithium (Li) and magnesium (Mg) is termed as 'diagonal relationship'. In the periodic table, some elements show similar properties with their diagonal neighbors due to comparable size, ionization energy, polarizing power, and electronic configuration. For example, Li (Group 1) and Mg (Group 2) both form similar oxides and carbonates (Li2O and MgO). This resemblance arises from their diagonal positions, not due to same Zeff, inert pair effect, or isoelectronic species.

Extra Facts:
1. Diagonal relationships are observed between second and third period elements, e.g., Be (Beryllium) and Al (Aluminum), B (Boron) and Si (Silicon).
2. This relationship occurs due to similar atomic size and charge/size ratio, leading to analogous chemical behavior.
3. Both Li and Mg directly react with nitrogen to form nitrides (Li3N and Mg3N2), unlike other Group 1 and Group 2 elements.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ Which elements show a diagonal relationship in the periodic table? → Li-Mg, Be-Al, B-Si
☛ Which element does lithium resemble in properties? → Magnesium
☛ What are isoelectronic species? → Ions/molecules with the same electronic configuration
☛ Inert pair effect is observed in which elements? → Heavy p-block elements (e.g., Pb, Sn)
☛ What is the relationship between Be and Al? → Diagonal relationship
question_hi:
लीथियम का व्यवहार मैग्नीशियम के व्यवहार के समान होता है। इस प्रकार की समानता को सामान्यतः _______कहा जाता है।

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: समान जेफ़ (same Zeff)
अक्रिय युग्म प्रभाव (inert pair effect)
समइलेक्ट्रॉनी स्पीशीज़ (isoelectronic species)
विकर्ण संबंध (diagonal relationship)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है विकर्ण संबंध (diagonal relationship)

Explanation:
लीथियम (Li) और मैग्नीशियम (Mg) के बीच समानता को 'विकर्ण संबंध' कहा जाता है। आवर्त सारणी में कुछ तत्व अपने विकर्ण (diagonal) पड़ोसी तत्वों के साथ समान गुण प्रदर्शित करते हैं। यह समानता उनके आकार (size), आयनन ऊर्जा (ionization energy), ध्रुवीकरण क्षमता (polarizing power), और इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास (electronic configuration) के कारण होती है। उदाहरण के लिए, Li (ग्रुप 1) और Mg (ग्रुप 2) दोनों ही ऑक्साइड और कार्बोनेट के रूप में समान यौगिक बनाते हैं, जैसे Li2O और MgO। यह समानता उनके विकर्ण स्थिति के कारण होती है, न कि समान जेफ़, अक्रिय युग्म प्रभाव, या समइलेक्ट्रॉनी स्पीशीज़ के कारण।

Extra Facts:
1. विकर्ण संबंध आवर्त सारणी के दूसरे और तीसरे अवधि (period) के तत्वों में देखा जाता है, जैसे Be (बेरिलियम) और Al (एल्युमिनियम), B (बोरॉन) और Si (सिलिकॉन)।
2. यह संबंध तत्वों के परमाणु आकार और आवेश/आकार अनुपात (charge/size ratio) के कारण होता है, जिससे उनकी रासायनिक प्रकृति समान हो जाती है।
3. लीथियम और मैग्नीशियम दोनों ही नाइट्रोजन के साथ सीधे प्रतिक्रिया करके नाइट्राइड (Li3N और Mg3N2) बनाते हैं, जो अन्य ग्रुप 1 और ग्रुप 2 तत्व नहीं करते।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

question:

Ferrum is the Latin name for iron, which has the chemical symbol Fe. Iron is an important metal used in construction, machinery, and various industries. question:
Identify an element that is NOT a semimetal.

[SSC GD 2022]

Germanium
Arsenic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Caesium

Explanation:
Semimetals (or metalloids) are elements that have properties intermediate between metals and nonmetals. Silicon (Si), Germanium (Ge), and Arsenic (As) are all semimetals because they exhibit both metallic and nonmetallic properties and are semiconductors. On the other hand, Caesium (Cs) is an alkali metal, which is purely metallic in nature. It is highly reactive and a good conductor of electricity, so it is not a semimetal.

Extra Facts:
Semimetals are located between metals and nonmetals in the periodic table. They are widely used in semiconductor devices like transistors, diodes, and solar cells. Silicon is the most commonly used semiconductor in the electronics industry. Germanium is used in optical fibers and infrared optics. Arsenic is used in semiconductors and pesticides. Caesium is used in atomic clocks and photoelectric cells due to its precise electron emission properties.

What happens to the atomic size as you go down the group?

solution:

Explanation:
The atomic size increases as you go down a group. This happens because, down the group, the number of electrons increases, and new electron shells (energy levels) are added. Each new shell increases the atomic size as electrons are placed farther from the nucleus. Additionally, the attractive force between the nucleus and electrons decreases due to increased distance, leading to an expansion in atomic size. This is one of the fundamental properties of the periodic table.

Extra Facts:
1. Atomic size decreases across a period (left to right) because the nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell, increasing the attractive force.
2. Ionic radius also increases down a group due to the addition of electron shells.
3. The smallest atom is hydrogen (H), while the largest naturally occurring atom is francium (Fr).

Explanation:

The elements in group zero are commonly known as 'Inert gases' or 'Noble gases'. These elements include Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), and Radon (Rn). The most important property of these gases is that they are highly stable and do not readily react with other elements. question:
Which law was based on notes of the music?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Newton law
Law of octaves
Mendeleev law
Modern periodic law
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Law of octaves

Explanation:
The Law of Octaves was based on the notes of music. This law was proposed by John Newlands in 1865. He observed that when elements were arranged in increasing order of their atomic weights, every eighth element had properties similar to the first, similar to how musical notes repeat after the eighth note (octave). However, this law worked only up to Calcium (Ca) and failed for heavier elements. Later, Mendeleev introduced a more refined version of the periodic table.

Extra Facts:
John Newlands' Law of Octaves is considered the first attempt to classify elements. It was inspired by the concept of musical notes, where the sequence repeats after the eighth note. However, this law had several limitations, such as not accounting for noble gases and failing to explain the existence of isotopes. Later, Mendeleev's Periodic Table addressed these shortcomings and provided a more scientific basis for element classification.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner

Explanation:
Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner was a German chemist who grouped elements into 'triads' in 1817. He observed that certain groups of three elements had similar physical and chemical properties. In these triads, the atomic weight of the middle element was approximately the average of the other two elements. For example, lithium (Li), sodium (Na), and potassium (K) form a triad. Dobereiner's work significantly contributed to the development of the periodic table.

Extra Facts:
Dobereiner's triads laid the foundation for the development of the modern periodic table. He also recognized chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), and iodine (I) as a triad. Although this theory did not apply to all known elements, it was a crucial step toward the classification of elements. Later, Mendeleev used this basis to construct his periodic table.

question:
The correct order of electron affinity of halogens is:

[SSC CHSL 2023]

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is I < Br < F

Explanation:
The correct order of electron affinity for halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) is Cl > F > Br > I. However, among the given options, the most accurate order is I < Br < F. Electron affinity is the energy released when an atom gains an extra electron. Fluorine (F) has lower electron affinity than chlorine (Cl) because fluorine's small size leads to greater electron-electron repulsion. Iodine (I) has the lowest electron affinity due to its large atomic size and weaker nuclear attraction.

Explanation:
Arsenic (As) is a metalloid element with atomic number 33. It belongs to group 15 (nitrogen group) of the periodic table. Its electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p³. Arsenic is a toxic element used in pesticides, semiconductor industry and some alloys. Among other options: Iodine (I) has atomic number 53, Neon (Ne) has 10 and Barium (Ba) has 56.

Extra Facts:
Arsenic is called the 'King of Poisons' as it was historically used as a poison. It doesn't occur free in nature but is found in minerals. Arsenic has two main allotropes - metallic arsenic and yellow arsenic. It's a major cause of water pollution. The most important ore of arsenic is arsenopyrite. Chronic arsenic poisoning causes skin lesions and cancer.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन से तत्व की परमाणु संख्या 33 है?

[SSC GD 2022]
options_hi: आयोडीन
नियॉन
बेरियम
आर्सेनिक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है आर्सेनिक

Explanation:
आर्सेनिक (As) एक धातु-जैसा तत्व है जिसकी परमाणु संख्या 33 है। यह आवर्त सारणी के समूह 15 (नाइट्रोजन समूह) में स्थित है। आर्सेनिक का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p³ है। यह एक विषैला तत्व है और इसका उपयोग कीटनाशकों, अर्धचालक उद्योग और कुछ मिश्र धातुओं में किया जाता है। अन्य विकल्पों में: आयोडीन (I) की परमाणु संख्या 53, नियॉन (Ne) की 10 और बेरियम (Ba) की 56 है।

Extra Facts:
आर्सेनिक को 'राजा का विष' भी कहा जाता है क्योंकि ऐतिहासिक रूप से इसका उपयोग जहर के रूप में किया जाता था। यह प्रकृति में मुक्त अवस्था में नहीं पाया जाता है बल्कि खनिजों के रूप में मिलता है। आर्सेनिक के दो मुख्य अपरूप होते हैं - धात्विक आर्सेनिक और पीला आर्सेनिक। यह जल प्रदूषण का एक प्रमुख कारक भी है।
